details: Bitcoin fell below $80,000 on Thursday, losing 2.4% to touch $79,720. This decline was driven by a sell-off in U.S. technology stocks, particularly in the AI sector due to signs of slowing revenue growth, which led to a broader risk-off sentiment. Additionally, hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data, including September's Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI), intensified concerns about further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. This macroeconomic environment reduced demand for higher-risk assets like cryptocurrencies and resulted in nearly $1 billion in crypto liquidations, with long positions bearing the brunt of the losses.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80K Amid AI Rout & Inflation Fears

details: The International Monetary Fund's (IMF) latest Global Financial Stability Report has recognized platforms like Ondo for their role in tokenization but concurrently cautioned that tokenized markets remain relatively illiquid and volatile. This report comes as the total crypto market capitalization saw a 2.39% decline over the last 24 hours, with Ondo (ONDO) specifically dropping about 5.96%. This volatility aligns with a broader de-risking trend in leveraged and spot positions, particularly affecting high-beta altcoins during periods of macro shock and inflation concerns.
title: IMF Highlights Tokenized Asset Volatility; ONDO Down 6%

details: European Central Bank (ECB) policymaker Alvaro Santos Pereira indicated that inflation is currently not spreading, and economic growth is showing surprising upside. Separately, ECB Governing Council member Primoz Dolenc suggested that if financial conditions tighten naturally in the markets, the central bank might not need to implement as many monetary policy actions as otherwise anticipated. These statements emerge amidst ongoing market repricing.
title: ECB Officials Hint at Less Aggressive Policy if Markets Tighten Naturally

details: Russia's Central Bank has announced that direct peer-to-peer (P2P) cryptocurrency transactions will be prohibited for its citizens starting July 1, 2027. Under new regulations, all cryptocurrency buying and selling must occur through state-regulated intermediaries. Retail investors will also face an annual purchase limit of 300,000 rubles (approximately $3,690) per intermediary, signifying a move towards stricter state control over crypto operations.
title: Russia to Ban Direct Peer-to-Peer Crypto Trades by July 2027
